page: The Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is a memory-focused virtual instance within Vultr's Optimized Cloud Compute family. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors, this instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores running with 2 threads per core at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16 extensions), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Resource allocation is centered around memory density, pairing the 4 vCPUs with 32.0 GB of RAM to deliver an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is directly integrated, offering a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD local drive, while networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this configuration.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread execution and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng single-core testing, the instance achieved a top-tier score of 3,434.57, matched by strong results in Geekbench single-core (2,149.0) and Geekbench text processing (2,828.0). Memory performance is robust, posting a strong PassMark memory score of 2,761.34 and large-block write bandwidth of 113.08 GB/s. However, multi-core metrics fall into the average band, with stress-ng multi-core recording 13,688.52 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 6,690.0. The server demonstrates weaker performance in static web throughput (3.81 GB/s) and multi-threaded decompression.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory profile and strong per-core computational throughput, the instance offers balanced cost efficiency for tasks requiring substantial memory residency without paying for excess compute cores. It is suited for in-memory caches, data processing pipelines, intermediate build environments, and moderate backend application services.
